author: JC
premise: A young second mate, on his first voyage with the rank, freezes during a squall and the captain takes the deck in his place. Nobody speaks of it afterwards. For the rest of the passage the mate watches the crew for any sign that they saw, and the captain for any sign that he will report it.
setting: A barque in the Indian Ocean, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An English railway engineer surveying a line through the mountains of a small republic is caught between the government that hired him and a rebel general who controls the passes. Both demand his loyalty, and each promises that the railway will bring civilisation.

author: JC
premise: A police inspector who has spent years cultivating informers among London's foreign revolutionaries is ordered by a new superior to make an arrest that will please the newspapers. The only man he can plausibly arrest is the informer who has kept him safe.

author: JC
premise: A Russian student living in exile in a Swiss city is approached by a revolutionary committee who believe him to be one of them. He is not, but their trust is the only warmth he has known since leaving home. He must decide how long he can let the mistake continue.

author: JC
premise: A surveyor sent to map a river for a concession company finds that the villages marked on his predecessor's chart do not exist, and never did. The company's directors in Europe have already sold shares on the strength of the chart. He must decide what his own map will show.

author: JC
premise: A captain whose ship has gone aground through his own error must give evidence at the inquiry. His mate, who warned him, is called next. The captain watches the mate in the witness box and waits to learn whether loyalty or truth will prevail.

author: JC
premise: A Basque sea captain who carries mail along the coast of a turbulent republic is ordered by a rebel commander to land a cargo of rifles at a fishing village. He has carried every kind of cargo for thirty years and never asked what was in a crate. This time he knows.
setting: A coastal steamer off a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A clerk at a foreign legation in London is ordered to burn a set of papers before an inspection. He reads them first, and learns that the legation has been paying an English member of Parliament. He keeps one sheet, and does not know why.

author: JC
premise: A Polish widow living in Paris receives a visit from a young man who claims to have shared a prison cell with her son in Warsaw. He brings the son's last message. She wants to believe him, and notices that he cannot meet her eyes.

author: JC
premise: A ship's carpenter is accused by the crew of stealing from the stores during a long calm. The captain believes him innocent but cannot prove it. As the calm continues and water runs short, the crew's suspicion hardens into something dangerous.
setting: A sailing ship becalmed in the Atlantic, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A hotel keeper in the capital of a small republic has served every president and every rebel who has ever taken a room. When two rival generals book the same floor on the same night, he must keep them from discovering each other until morning.
setting: A hotel in a South American capital, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A watchmaker in a London back street repairs timepieces for respectable customers and is asked one evening to repair a device whose purpose he guesses at once. The customer pays in advance. The watchmaker must decide whether to do the work, refuse it, or go to the police.

author: JC
premise: A Russian railway official who has always prided himself on having no politics is ordered to delay a train carrying a political prisoner, so that the prisoner's comrades may attempt a rescue. The order comes from his own brother.

author: JC
premise: A missionary and a trader share a small island station. They despise each other's work and depend on each other's company. When the trader's supply boat fails to arrive, they are left alone together for six months.
setting: An island in the Malay Archipelago, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A young captain on his first command takes on board a stranger who swims to the ship at night and confesses he has killed a man. The captain hides him in his cabin, and the secret binds them together in a way the captain cannot explain.
setting: A ship anchored in the Gulf of Siam, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A British consul in a small republic, who has spent twenty years writing reports nobody reads, receives a telegram announcing that a warship is coming to protect British interests. He realises he no longer knows what the British interests are, or whether he still shares them.

author: JC
premise: A railway porter at a London terminus finds a parcel left in the cloak room that ticks. The police are slow to come. He carries it out to an empty siding himself, and afterwards cannot explain to his wife or to the newspapers why he did it.

author: JC
premise: A Swiss pastor whose congregation includes several Russian exiles is asked by one of them to perform a marriage without asking questions. The groom gives a false name. The pastor must decide whether a sacrament can rest on a lie.

author: JC
premise: A harbour pilot who once refused to take a ship out in a storm, against the owner's demand, learns years later that the owner has become chairman of the harbour board. The pilot is summoned to the board to explain a minor delay.

author: JC
premise: A ship chandler in a port of a South American republic is entrusted by the departing English consul with the consulate's archives. When a revolutionary colonel demands them, the chandler must decide whether a few boxes of paper are worth his life.
setting: A port in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A middle-aged anarchist who has lived for years on the subscriptions of wealthy sympathisers is introduced to a young lady who wishes to give him her fortune. He realises, for the first time, that he does not believe in anything.
setting: A drawing room in Mayfair, London, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A revolutionary agent sent from Russia to assassinate a minister abroad falls ill on the journey and is nursed by a family of Swiss peasants. Their simple decency disturbs him more than any argument he has heard against his cause.
setting: A village in the Swiss Alps, 1900s

author: JC
premise: A Dutch trader who has lived thirty years among the people of a remote river settlement is visited by a young Englishman seeking to buy his business. The old man shows him the river and the people, and the Englishman cannot tell whether he is being welcomed or warned.

author: JC
premise: A ship's master falls ill on a long voyage, and the first mate takes command. When the master recovers and wishes to resume command, the mate, who has proved a better seaman, must decide whether to surrender it.
setting: A clipper in the South Atlantic, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A general who has seized power in a small republic invites the foreign merchants to a banquet to reassure them. A young lieutenant of his guard, who has seen what happened in the provinces, serves the wine and listens.
setting: A presidential palace in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A young typist employed by a revolutionary journal in London discovers that its editor is in the pay of a foreign police. She must decide whether to expose him and destroy the journal she believes in, or keep silent and keep her place.
setting: A printing office in Islington, London, 1900s

author: JC
premise: A Russian countess living in a Swiss pension is visited by her husband's former secretary, who announces that he has joined the revolutionaries and wishes her to finance them. She has no sympathy with the revolution and a great deal for him.

author: JC
premise: A shipwrecked crew in an open boat must decide whether to make for the nearest land, where natives are reported hostile, or a distant port. The captain, who is dying, will not decide. The mate and the bosun cannot agree.
setting: An open boat in the Java Sea, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An English engineer's wife living on a coffee estate in the hills of a South American republic befriends the local priest, the only educated man within fifty miles. When revolution reaches the valley, her husband forbids the priest the house.
setting: A coffee estate in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: An informer for the police is shadowed through London by a revolutionary who suspects him. Each knows what the other is. Neither can act. They end the evening drinking in the same public house, each waiting for the other to make the first move.

author: JC
premise: A Russian student accused by the exiles of being a police spy must prove his innocence to a committee that has already decided his guilt. The only witness who could clear him is the man who denounced him.

author: JC
premise: A company agent at an upriver station receives orders to abandon it and return to the coast. The local chief who has protected the station begs him to stay. The agent, who has grown attached to the place, must decide whose orders he will follow.
setting: An upriver station in Central Africa, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A captain discovers that his chief officer has been secretly drinking, and that the ship's course has been wrongly reckoned for a week. Reporting the officer will ruin him. Not reporting him may lose the ship.
setting: A steamer in the Red Sea, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A young engineer working on a harbour scheme in a South American port falls in love with the daughter of a local politician. When her father joins a revolt, the engineer must decide whether to stay in the port or take the last steamer home.
setting: A port city in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A respectable bookseller in a quiet London street keeps a back room where foreign exiles meet. His wife has always pretended not to know. When the police come to the shop, she discovers how much she does know.

author: JC
premise: A Russian revolutionary who has spent ten years in Siberia escapes and reaches Switzerland, where the exiles hail him as a living legend. He finds that he no longer believes in the revolution, and that he cannot tell them so.

author: JC
premise: A seaman who gave false evidence at an inquiry to protect his captain finds, years later, that the captain has died and left him a small legacy in gratitude. He must decide whether he can accept money that feels like payment for a lie.

author: JC
premise: A fisherman's widow on a coast of a turbulent republic finds a drowned soldier on the beach with a satchel of letters. Some are addressed to the government, some to the rebels. She cannot read, and must decide whom to trust to read them for her.
setting: A fishing village on a South American coast, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A cabinet minister's private secretary is approached by an old school friend, now an anarchist, who asks for a meeting with the minister. The secretary agrees, believing he can bring about reconciliation. The friend has other intentions.

author: JC
premise: A young Russian translator employed by a Swiss publishing house is asked to translate the memoirs of a revolutionary who denounces the translator's late father as a police agent. He does not know whether the accusation is true.

author: JC
premise: An English clerk in a remote trading post is left in charge when the manager dies of fever. He has no experience and no orders. The local traders test him daily, and he begins to understand how the manager kept his authority.
setting: A trading post in the Congo, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A ship's boy who survived a wreck in which the captain went down with the ship is asked by the captain's widow to tell her how her husband died. The boy knows the captain died a coward. He must decide what to tell her.

author: JC
premise: A customs officer in a South American port is offered a fortune to look away while a ship is loaded at night. He has been honest all his life and poor all his life. His wife is ill, and the ship sails at dawn.

author: JC
premise: A young woman whose brother has been arrested as an anarchist goes to the police to plead for him, and finds the inspector both courteous and immovable. She returns the next day, and the next. Something in her persistence troubles the inspector.

author: JC
premise: An exile in Geneva receives a letter from his mother in Russia, begging him to return and accept the Tsar's pardon. The revolutionaries regard such letters as police tricks. He does not know whether his mother wrote it.

author: JC
premise: A ship carrying a cargo of coal catches fire below decks. The captain decides to keep sailing for port rather than abandon her. The crew work for days fighting a fire they cannot see, and the ship's young third mate learns what endurance means.
setting: A barque in the Indian Ocean, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A priest in a mountain village of a South American republic hides the treasure of his church from a revolutionary army. The colonel who comes to find it was once his altar boy.
setting: A mountain village in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A doctor who treats the poor of the East End is consulted secretly by an anarchist who has been injured making a bomb. The doctor's oath obliges him to treat the man. His conscience demands that he inform the police.

author: JC
premise: A Russian girl who has come to Switzerland to study medicine is drawn into the circle of the exiles by a charismatic speaker. Her fellow student, a quiet Pole, warns her against him. She suspects the warning is jealousy.

author: JC
premise: A harbour master in a small Eastern port is ordered by the colonial government to refuse entry to a ship flying no flag. Its captain sends ashore a letter in a hand the harbour master recognises: his own brother's, whom he has not seen in twenty years.
setting: A port in the Dutch East Indies, 1890s

author: JC
premise: An old sea captain who has lost his sight hides it from his owners and his crew, relying on his mate to read the instruments for him. The mate is ambitious, and the owners are suspicious.
setting: A coasting steamer in the Gulf of Siam, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A newspaper editor in the capital of a small republic writes an article praising a revolt. The revolt fails. He must decide whether to flee, recant, or wait for the soldiers.

author: JC
premise: A retired police informer who has lived for years on a small pension from the Home Office is recognised in a London street by a man he once betrayed, now returned from prison. The man greets him warmly and asks him to dinner.

author: JC
premise: An old Russian general who once crushed a rising in Poland lives in exile in a Swiss hotel. A young Polish woman takes a room on the same floor. He knows why she has come.

author: JC
premise: A ship's crew mutinies against a brutal captain. The second mate, who shares their hatred of the captain, must decide whether to join them or stand by the man he despises.
setting: A sailing ship in the Pacific, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An Englishwoman who runs a school for girls in a South American port is asked by a revolutionary leader to teach his daughter. She agrees, and finds herself regarded by both sides as a traitor.
setting: A port city in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A professor of political economy who has written in favour of revolution is visited by a young man who intends to put the professor's ideas into practice. The professor is horrified, and must decide whether his ideas were ever meant to be acted upon.

author: JC
premise: A Russian revolutionary living in London receives orders to return to Russia and carry out an assassination. His English wife does not know what he is. On the night before he leaves, she asks him why he seems so far away.

author: JC
premise: A mining engineer who has spent years building a railway into the mountains of a republic, believing it would bring prosperity to the villages along its route, stands on the platform at the coast to watch the first train arrive. It is carrying soldiers.

author: JC
premise: A captain who has spent his life on sailing ships is given command of a steamer. He distrusts the engines and the engineers. When the engines fail in a storm, he must rely on the men he has despised.
setting: A steamer in the Bay of Biscay, 1890s
